name: Lexington Law
description_short: Lexington Law is a credit repair law firm that disputes errors and negative items on credit reports using licensed attorneys and paralegals. They've served nearly 11 million clients since 2004.
description_long:
Lexington Law was founded in 2004 and operates as a credit repair law firm specializing in disputing inaccurate or unverifiable items on consumer credit reports. The company leverages a team of licensed attorneys and skilled paralegals to challenge negative marks across the major credit bureaus. With over 20 years in the industry, Lexington Law has become one of the larger players in the credit repair space, positioning itself as "America's #1 Credit Improvement Law Firm."

The company's core service involves disputing negative items on credit reports, including collections, late payments, charge-offs, repossessions, foreclosures, bankruptcies, judgments, medical bills, and hard inquiries. Clients receive a personalized credit assessment at no cost to start, with the first payment due five days after sign-up. The service includes monthly FICO score updates from TransUnion, a mobile app for tracking progress, personalized score improvement strategies, $1M identity theft insurance coverage, and phone support. Lexington Law also provides educational content on credit repair, credit laws, and dispute processes through their blog and resource library.

Lexington Law distinguishes itself through its use of licensed attorneys rather than just paralegals, formal agreements with credit bureaus, and four U.S. Patents awarded by the Patent and Trademark Office for their proprietary credit repair strategies. The company reports 84 million total removals since 2004, with breakdowns showing over 50 million collections removed, 13 million late payments, and 9.5 million charge-offs. They advertise that 50% of negative items are removed within 6 months for moderately damaged credit profiles (those with fewer than four negative items) who remain active clients. There are no long-term contracts, allowing clients to cancel anytime.

However, several important caveats apply. Lexington Law explicitly states they can only "communicate with creditors on your behalf and verify report changes with bureaus"—they do not guarantee specific removals, and results vary significantly by case. The cited statistic of "50% removal in 6 months" applies only to a specific subset of clients with moderate damage who stay active. Testimonials are presented as individual results, with a disclaimer that "your case is different than everyone else's." Clients should understand they are paying for dispute services, not guaranteed credit score improvements, and the company's legal approach relies on enforcing consumer protection laws rather than removing legitimately reported accurate items.
pros: Licensed attorneys and paralegals on staff, not just dispute processors
No cost to start—first payment due 5 days after sign-up, allowing risk-free evaluation
Monthly FICO score updates from TransUnion included in service
Four U.S. Patents awarded for proprietary credit repair strategies
Mobile app for real-time progress tracking
Formal agreements with multiple credit bureaus
cons: Results highly variable; the advertised "50% removal in 6 months" applies only to moderately damaged credit profiles that remain active, not all clients
Company only guarantees communication and verification, not actual item removals—cannot remove accurate, timely reported negative items
Ongoing monthly fees required; costs not clearly disclosed on homepage, requiring sign-up for pricing
Large client volume (11 million served) may impact personalization and individual attention
Testimonials are limited and present only positive cases; no data on success rates or average outcomes
best_for: Consumers with moderately damaged credit (3-5 negative items) seeking attorney-backed dispute support
People with potential errors or unverifiable items on their credit reports who want legal advocacy
Those who prefer ongoing attorney involvement rather than DIY disputes or non-legal credit repair services
Consumers willing to pay monthly fees for professional dispute management and score monitoring
diagnosis: Lexington Law is best for consumers with moderate credit damage (3-5 negative items) who want attorney-backed dispute support and are willing to pay monthly fees for ongoing professional representation. The critical caveat is that results vary significantly by case, removal rates apply only to specific client segments, and the company cannot remove accurate, legitimately reported negative items—they can only dispute and verify based on consumer protection laws.
services: Credit report disputes for errors and inaccurate items
Bankruptcy, foreclosure, and repossession dispute services
Free initial credit assessment and FICO score review
Educational resources on credit laws and dispute processes
